symbols.name: chunk-width exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent giving the chunk width K = floor(d^c); not the machine constant.
symbols.quote: The axis count is $d=\Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ and the chunk width $K=\lfloor d^{c}\rfloor$, with fixed exponents $\epsilon$ and $c$ from [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md); here $c$ is not the machine constant.

relations.quote: Power-saving integer multiplication is the main result: for $n$, the number of bits in each input, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$, a fixed Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, which is $o(n\log n)$, so it refutes the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) in this model.

The exact $2n$-bit product is assembled by [The multiplication algorithm](multiplication-algorithm.md) from radix digits, two forward transforms, a pointwise product, the opposite transform, rescaling, rounding and carries, with total error below $1/2$.

relations.predicate: has its running time totaled by
relations.quote: [Cost accounting and the exponent κ](cost-accounting.md) totals the running time as follows, dividing every cost by $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, the number of stored bits, where $T$ counts coefficients and $p$, of order $\lg n$, is the precision in bits of each.
